slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Lev 1:2-9: a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
slides.body: “a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.”
slides.heading: Lev 1:2-9

slides.alt_text: Slide 1: The ritual phrase and its Christological reuse.
slides.body: Leviticus calls a burnt offering 'a pleasing aroma to the LORD'. Ephesians calls Christ's self-giving a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.
slides.heading: A fragrant sacrifice

slides.body: A named commentator links Ephesians to Leviticus 1:9. Christians can see Christ's self-giving as a culmination of accepted-offering imagery.
slides.heading: An intentional connection

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Recurrence and original ritual function.
slides.body: Leviticus gives rules for repeated offerings; the aroma phrase occurs elsewhere too. Ephesians reuses the image, but Leviticus 1 alone is not a unique prediction.
slides.heading: A recurring formula
